identification.summary: North Korean actor within the Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB) that conducts cyber espionage against military, defense and technology targets to advance the regime's military and nuclear programs, and that has expanded into financial gain, including ransomware [S1][S2]. A US indictment unsealed in July 2024 charged an alleged member for Maui ransomware attacks on US hospitals [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft first observed the actor in 2014 [S1]; MITRE: active since at least 2009 [S4]. TigerRAT in use since 2020 [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Onyx Sleet (formerly PLUTONIUM). Microsoft maps SILENT CHOLLIMA, StoneFly, DarkSeoul, Andariel and APT45 to it [S5]; MITRE tracks it as Andariel (G0138) [S4]. These names were previously merged into the Diamond Sleet (Lazarus) record and have been separated.

attribution.sponsor: Democratic People's Republic of Korea: Reconnaissance General Bureau [S2].
attribution.confidence: Formal US government attribution through the indictment of Rim Jong Hyok, announced 25 Jul 2024, which describes him as an RGB member associated with Andariel / Onyx Sleet / APT45 [S2]. Microsoft attributes the activity to Onyx Sleet [S1].
attribution.basis: DOJ indictment and FBI investigation [S2]; Microsoft telemetry [S1]; CISA-linked advisory reporting cited by Microsoft [S1].

objectives: Intelligence collection supporting DPRK military and nuclear programs, primarily from military, defense and technology targets [S1]. Revenue generation through ransomware and possibly online gambling [S1][S2], with ransom proceeds laundered through Hong Kong-based facilitators [S2].

sectors: Military and defense (including US defense contractors and US Air Force bases)
targeting.notes: Regions and sectors from Microsoft [S1]. FBI-reported victims: five healthcare providers, four US defense contractors, two US Air Force bases and NASA OIG [S2].

capabilities.summary: Custom malware including TigerRAT (since 2020), SmallTiger (against South Korean defense and manufacturing), LightHand, ValidAlpha/BlackRAT and Dtrack [S1]. Custom ransomware, notably Maui, used against US hospitals [S1][S2]. MITRE lists 12 techniques for Andariel (G0138), including gh0st RAT and Rifdoor usage [S4]. The MITRE mapping is thin relative to the public reporting, so treat the ATT&CK list as incomplete.

campaigns.name: Maui ransomware against US healthcare
campaigns.summary: RGB-developed Maui ransomware encrypted medical testing and records systems at US hospitals; ransoms laundered via Hong Kong facilitators. Charged in the 2024 indictment.

campaigns.name: Indictment of Rim Jong Hyok
campaigns.summary: Kansas grand jury charges for conspiracy to commit computer hacking and money laundering; $10M reward; added to FBI Most Wanted. Victims include defense contractors, US Air Force bases and NASA OIG.

campaigns.name: TigerRAT / SmallTiger espionage
campaigns.summary: Custom RATs against defense, manufacturing and technology targets, primarily in South Korea, the US and India.

diamond.adversary: RGB operators; Rim Jong Hyok charged in 2024 [S2].
diamond.capability: TigerRAT, SmallTiger, LightHand, ValidAlpha, Dtrack; Maui ransomware [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Actor-controlled C2; cryptocurrency ransom payment and laundering through Hong Kong facilitators [S2].
diamond.victim: Defense contractors, military installations, NASA OIG, US hospitals, South Korean defense and manufacturing, Indian targets [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Support to DPRK military and nuclear programs, plus sanctions-evading revenue [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Vulnerable internet-facing systems and weak healthcare IT resilience exploited for ransomware leverage [S2].

gaps: Primary indictment PDF and the joint technical advisory issued alongside it were not fetched (government sites blocked); the advisory identifier should be confirmed.
MITRE's Andariel technique list (12) is far smaller than the reported tradecraft; analyst mapping from Microsoft and advisory reporting is needed.
How ransomware revenue and espionage tasking are balanced within the group is not public.
Overlap with the Diamond Sleet record's historical 'Lazarus' events (e.g. DarkSeoul) should be reconciled.

Primary-source check (2026-10-18): DOJ release confirms Rim Jong Hyok (RGB, Andariel/Onyx Sleet/APT45), Maui ransomware, laundering through Hong Kong facilitators, the funded intrusions into defense contractors, Air Force bases and NASA-OIG, Log4Shell access, and the $10M reward. It gives no victim counts, no online-gambling link, no TigerRAT/SmallTiger/Dtrack, and says a grand jury returned the indictment on 24 July (announced 25 July).

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: The OE includes DIB contractors, military installations' IT and healthcare systems supporting military communities. This actor targets all three. STEP 2: Ransomware against hospitals near installations can degrade medical support to forces and families. STEP 3: The template is exploitation of internet-facing systems, then custom RATs for espionage, and in some cases ransomware deployment for revenue. STEP 4: MLCOA is persistent espionage against defense and aerospace technology to support weapons programs. MDCOA is ransomware against healthcare or installation-support providers during a Korean Peninsula crisis, combining revenue with disruption. Candidate indicators: TigerRAT or SmallTiger detections, ransomware staging in healthcare networks, and intrusions at aerospace and defense suppliers [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Coordinate with USFK and INDOPACOM, and with South Korean partners, since South Korea is the primary target. (2) Include Defense Health Agency and community hospital partners in situational awareness for ransomware threats. (3) Financial disruption (seizures, sanctions) is a DOJ and Treasury lead but affects the actor's resources; track it as part of campaign assessment. (4) DIB CS program reporting is a primary sensor for this actor's espionage.

provenance.importedSummary:
Andariel is a North Korean state-sponsored threat group that has been active since at least 2009. Andariel has primarily focused its operations--which have included destructive attacks--against South Korean government agencies, military organizations, and a variety of domestic companies; they have also conducted cyber financial operations against ATMs, banks, and cryptocurrency exchanges. Andariel's notable activity includes Operation Black Mine, Operation GoldenAxe, and Campaign Rifle.

Andariel is considered a sub-set of Lazarus Group, and has been attributed to North Korea's Reconnaissance General Bureau.

North Korean group definitions are known to have significant overlap, and some security researchers report all North Korean state-sponsored cyber activity under the name Lazarus Group instead of tracking clusters or subgroups.
